_README: Provenance record for every number printed in report/report.tex.
Checked by experiments/verify_report.py. One entry per printed value:
id      -- stable name, used by --only
tex     -- line of report.tex the literal sits on (fix with --resync)
literal -- exact substring of that line; its absence means the report
was edited away from this manifest
printed -- the value as printed, in printed units
unit    -- raw | pct (artifact x100) | deg_from_periods (x360)
vs      -- if present, printed value is (artifact/vs - 1)*100
tol     -- absolute, in printed units; set to HALF THE LAST PRINTED
DIGIT, so a number that would round differently fails
src     -- the artifact, key and reduction that regenerates it
src.kind == 'manual' means the number has no machine-readable artifact.
Those are listed as UNCHECKED, never as passing. Every one of them is a
gap to close, not a number to trust.
Convention note: every seed-averaged table in the report says 'seed
means', so reduce is 'mean' throughout. Where a row only reconciles
under 'max' (the worse seed), that is recorded as a MISMATCH rather than
papered over by changing the reducer, because the caption would then be
wrong.

entries.note: Reference is Qu et al. (2013) Table 3 at Re = 100, Cd = 1.317 -- a single citable value, used consistently for all three Cd errors in this section. Their Table 1 range across eight studies is 1.318 to 1.336. The previous uncited '1.37-1.38' benchmark was wrong and hid a systematic overshoot.
Now the VORTICITY St, consistent with sec:acoustic, which states the lift is not trusted for frequency. The lift value for this dataset is 0.1611.
Against Qu et al. (2013) Table 3, St = 0.1649 at Re = 100, rather than the round 0.165 used before.

Convention now stated in the report: interior_mask(halo=2, edge=2) with an r.m.s. norm. The halo sweep in runs/derived_metrics.json shows the figure ranges from 4.08 % (halo 0) to 0.53 % (halo 8), so the convention is load-bearing and must stay in the caption.

Two-point linear extrapolation through the 2.5% and 3.3% cases. The three-point set is strongly non-linear, so this choice must be stated in the report; a three-point least-squares fit gives a different intercept.

Every other seed-averaged table in the report says 'seed means', so the reducer here is kept as mean and the disagreement is surfaced. src.provenance: NO ARTIFACT, and confirmed unrecoverable on 2026-09-22. The GPU server holds only the REGENERATED datasets (cylinder_re60_v1 at u = 0.0277), whose metadata is now committed under data/; the superseded u = 0.05 run that produced the locked wake was overwritten in place. The 0.114 and 0.113 figures are therefore the only two numbers in this report that rest on a measurement nothing can reproduce. Everything ELSE in the acoustic section is now derived: the resonance frequency, the separations and the St/St_a ratios all come from runs/derived_metrics.json. Options: re-run the two datasets at u = 0.05 to restore the measurement (cheap -- minutes on the GPU), or state in the text that these two values are reported from a run that was not archived.
NO ARTIFACT. Same as acoustic.locked.St60, and recoverable the same way.

entries.note: The largest Cl_rms in the convergence sweep is 0.558 (D=32), which rounds to 0.56, not 0.54. Either the range is quoted from a subset or 0.54 is a slip. SEPARATELY: the '~0.23' benchmark in the same sentence is CORRECT and now citable -- Qu et al. (2013) Table 1 gives Cl' = 0.222-0.235 across eight Re=100 studies, with 0.2224 at H=120. The v4 dataset's 0.1774 is about 20% below that, consistent with the report's own statement that Cl rms is not converged.
